question: Why do standard health clinics often fail to reach young people effectively?
explanation: Many young people avoid standard clinics because staff members can be unwelcoming or judgmental about youth sexuality. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T6#BMP320_U3_T6_h1)

question: How do school and community programs mainly improve adolescent reproductive health?

options.A: By taking health information and services directly to where youths live and study
options.B: By replacing traditional school subjects entirely with medicine
options.C: By banning young people from using mobile phones
options.D: By forcing all teenagers to visit a hospital every single month

explanation: Bringing services to schools and communities removes the travel and fear barriers that keep youths away from clinics. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T6#BMP320_U3_T6_h1)

question: Which school program component uses trained students to lead discussions and share health messages?
explanation: Peer education clubs empower students to talk to their fellow classmates because young people often prefer listening to people their own age. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T6#BMP320_U3_T6_h2)

question: A female student asks a school health corner for confidential advice about painful menstruation. What is the best immediate action?

options.A: Report her behavior immediately to the school principal for punishment
options.B: Provide a private consultation and basic support or referral if needed
options.C: Ignore her request because menstruation is not a health issue
options.D: Announce her medical condition during the morning school assembly

explanation: School health corners exist to offer confidential guidance and connect students to proper care without fear of public embarrassment. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T6#BMP320_U3_T6_h2)

question: Who are key community gatekeepers that midwives must engage for successful youth health programs?
explanation: Local leaders hold immense influence over community attitudes, making their buy-in crucial for accepting reproductive health topics. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T6#BMP320_U3_T6_h3)

question: Why is it important to reach out-of-school adolescents through community programs?

options.A: Because they automatically know more about health than students
options.B: Because they do not live in any community setting
options.C: Because they are legally banned from ever learning about health
options.D: Because they miss out on health education delivered strictly inside classrooms

explanation: Adolescents who have dropped out of school or never attended miss school-based programs, so community initiatives are their primary lifeline. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T6#BMP320_U3_T6_h3)

question: What is a common misconception raised by critics against youth reproductive health education?

options.A: It is mandatory for elderly citizens
options.B: It instantly cures all infectious diseases
options.D: It replaces the need for clean drinking water

explanation: A widespread fear among conservative groups is that teaching young people about reproductive health will promote early sexual activity. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T6#BMP320_U3_T6_h4)

question: How should health educators best respond to community resistance regarding reproductive health topics?

options.A: Through transparent dialogue focused on health, safety, and responsible choices
options.B: By insulting the religious beliefs of community elders publicly
options.C: By shutting down all health clinics in the affected region
options.D: By ignoring local complaints and forcing programs through without discussion

explanation: Respectful communication and framing programs around wellness help ease fears and build trust with skeptical community members. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T6#BMP320_U3_T6_h4)

question: Which of the following describes a key clinical duty of a midwife in youth health?

options.A: Passing new national laws in the legislative assembly
options.B: Managing commercial transport businesses for youths
options.C: Providing counseling and managing minor reproductive infections
options.D: Building primary school classrooms with brick and mortar

explanation: Midwives use their clinical training to offer direct health services, counseling, and treatment for common adolescent health concerns. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T6#BMP320_U3_T6_h5)

question: A teenage girl visits a midwife's clinic, expressing great fear that her parents will find out. What must the midwife ensure?

options.A: Refusing to speak with the teenager until her parents arrive
options.B: Strict confidentiality to maintain the adolescent's trust
options.C: Immediate public announcement of the visit at the village square
options.D: Informing every teacher at the girl's school immediately

explanation: Assuring privacy and confidentiality is the single most important factor in encouraging young people to seek professional healthcare. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T6#BMP320_U3_T6_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of monitoring and evaluation in public health programs?

options.A: To punish health workers who fail to arrive early
options.B: To track program indicators and see if goals are being met
options.C: To prevent community members from asking questions
options.D: To increase the cost of medical drugs for patients

explanation: Monitoring and evaluation helps measure progress, identify weaknesses, and guide adjustments to make interventions more effective. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T6#BMP320_U3_T6_h6)

question: Why is relying solely on short-term international donor grants dangerous for health program sustainability?

options.A: Foreign grants automatically eliminate all cultural barriers
options.B: Donors always force health workers to close down schools permanently
options.C: International money cannot be converted into local Nigerian currency
options.D: Programs may collapse abruptly when the donor funding cycle ends

explanation: Sustainable programs require local ownership and domestic budget integration so they continue running after external partners leave. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T6#BMP320_U3_T6_h6)
